newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil - Peso drop seen dragging down market.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil - Peso drop seen dragging down market.

text.p: Coconut oil prices, which fell by an average of $40 per tonne CIF last week, are expected to fall further following the plunge of the peso and improving supplies from the Philippines, Manila vegetable oil traders said on Monday.
"Prices might fall below the psychological $600 per tonne CIF this year," said one senior trader.
Traders said the fall of the peso following Friday's announcement by the Central Bank of a de facto devaluation would also compel more sellers from the Philippines.
The trader said he expected coconut oil prices in Rotterdam to drop between $10 and $15 this week after closing at $600 to $602.50 per tonne CIF on Friday.
Demand for coconut oil is expected to remain thin this week even as stocks dwindled to 3,340 tonnes as of July 7 from the week-ago 8,148.
"I don't smell panic in the air despite low supplies due to the proposed arrival of six vessels carrying some 100,000 tonnes of coconut oil in the next two weeks," said one trader.
"Most of these shipments, however, have already been taken," he added.
Traders also said they expected more stocks from the Philippines in August, which is historically the highest month in terms of copra harvests.
